subject: general
question: Which movement is called India's first Civil Disobedience Movement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Champaran Movement of 1917 is considered India's first civil disobedience movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It was initiated to address the grievances of the farmers who were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions by the British planters.
 
• Gandhi's involvement in the movement marked his first significant experiment with non-violent resistance or Satyagraha in India.
 
• The success of the Champaran Movement laid the foundation for future civil disobedience campaigns against British rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement**

 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, it aimed at non-violent resistance to British rule by boycotting British goods, institutions, and services.
 
• The movement saw widespread participation and led to several significant events, including the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
 
 
• **Khilafat Movement**
 
 
• A pan-Islamist movement launched in 1919 to protest against the dismemberment of the Ottoman Caliphate by the British after World War I.
 
• Gandhi supported the movement to bring Hindu-Muslim unity in the struggle against British colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Kheda Movement**
 
 
• Another significant peasant movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1918 in Gujarat.
 
• It was launched to support farmers who were unable to pay taxes due to crop failure and sought remission of taxes.
